legend: Lipoblastoma-like tumour grows as a distinctly multinodular mass separated by intervening fibrous septate (A) often with a minor component of admixed mature adipose tissue (B).

LLT is a bland spindle cell neoplasm set in a wispy fibromyxoid to variably collagenized stroma supported by a striking plexiform, delicately arborizing vascular tree in which lipoblasts may either be (A) focal or (B) plentiful but are often concentrated (C) towards the periphery of the lobules. Lipoblasts in lipoblastoma-like tumour (D) are optically clear univacuoluated (ice cream cone) or bivacuolated (hourglass) in appearance.

Additional patterns in lipoblastoma-like tumour include (A) pulmonary oedema-like / lymphangioma-like microcystic spaces and (B) chronic inflammation that may be so extensive to obscure the basic underlying architecture.
